Your privacy

What Letterman keeps about you

Letterman is the learning portal of the Heirloom Estate Academy. This page says what it keeps about you, why, who can see it, how long it stays, and how to take it with you or erase it.

The short version

  • You never need an account to learn. Every week opens for a guest.
  • Nothing of yours is kept until you say yes.
  • Accounts are for people 13 or older.
  • Your work is seen by you and your teacher. Other students do not see it, and a gold star is seen only by you and the teacher who gave it.
  • You can export everything kept on your account, and erase it, whenever you like.
  • Letterman has no ads and adds no tracking or analytics.

As a guest

Without an account, nothing about you goes to Letterman's service. If you say yes to keeping your answers, they are kept in this browser, on this device, and nowhere else. The name you type as a guest is kept there too.

While a page of the course is open in front of you, it asks the service every 15 seconds whether a class of the course is live, so it can show the Live button. That question carries nothing of yours. If you press Live, your page keeps one connection open to follow the class's step, and closes it when you leave the live class or the page. A guest following a class is never on the teacher's list of who is here, and nothing about you is kept.

Every home page, a guest's included, shows the classes open for joining, and a guest can read their teachers' announcements. To show them, the page reads the two public lists (the open classes and their announcements) from Letterman's service. Those requests carry nothing of yours (no name, no answers, no sign-in), and nothing about you is stored. Like any website, the service records the request itself.

Settings and your data, inside Letterman, lets you save your answers to a file, load them on another device, or erase them.

As a guest you can also read the class's conversation about each module. It lives on Discord; Letterman's service reads it from there and shows it to you. Reading it sends nothing of yours.

If you share a hand-in to the class's Discord yourself, it goes to Discord, and Discord's own rules apply there.

With an account

For a student, signing in is a choice. It keeps your progress with you on any device, and lets you join a class, hand in your work, hear back from your teacher and write in the class's conversation. Teachers sign in to reach the teaching half of Letterman.

You sign in with Discord, or with a code sent to your email address.

Nothing is kept before you say yes

Before Letterman keeps anything of yours, it asks you two things: that you are 13 or older, and that you agree to it keeping your work. Until you say yes to both, nothing of yours is kept, and no work can be saved.

Letterman can only ask once you have signed in, so for that moment your sign-in itself (your email address, or your Discord account) is held. If you choose "Not now", that sign-in is erased at once. If you simply leave, it is erased within a day.

On your device, too, nothing lasting is kept before your yes: until then your sign-in is held only in the open tab, and goes when you close it. If you press Join before you have signed in, the open tab also remembers which class, so it can ask you once you have; that goes when you close the tab too. After your yes, this browser keeps your sign-in so that you stay signed in, until you sign out.

No one under 13 may make an account.

Your name is not your account

Your account has an id that Letterman uses inside the service. It never shows and never changes. Your display name is the name you choose, and you can change it at any time. Everything kept hangs on the id, so when you change your name it changes everywhere it shows in Letterman at once, and nothing is lost or split. Two people may choose the same name.

What is kept, why, and who can see it

Your sign-in

Your email address or, if you use Discord, what Discord shares with the sign-in: your Discord id, user name, picture and email address.

Why: so you can sign in again.
Who can see it: you. Your teacher does not.

Your display name

The name you choose.

Why: so your teacher knows whose work is whose.
Who can see it: you, and the teacher of each class you join or hand in to. Classmates do not see it in Letterman. If you teach, the students who can join your classes see yours.

Your two yeses

That you said you are 13 or older and said yes to keeping your work, and when.

Why: so it is clear Letterman asked first.
Who can see it: you.

Your progress

Where you are in each module and the answers you have made there.

Why: so your work follows you between devices. You can switch this off in Settings and your data ("Carry my work between devices"). When you first sign in on a device that already holds answers, Letterman asks before bringing them into your account.
Who can see it: you. Not your teacher, not anyone else.

The classes you join

Which classes, and when you joined.

Why: so your classes are in front of you, and your teacher knows who has joined.
Who can see it: you and that class's teacher.

Your hand-ins

The text you write and any link you add. No file is uploaded to Letterman.

Why: so your teacher can read your work and reply.
Who can see it: you and the teacher of the class you handed in to.

Answers you send in a live class

An answer you commit in the class's module while you follow your class live (you pressed Live). Only a class you joined: following someone else's class sends nothing.

Why: so your teacher sees the class's answers as they come in.
Who can see it: you and that class's teacher.

While you follow your class live, your teacher's console also shows that you are here, by your display name. That is not kept: it goes when you leave the live class or close the page.

Replies and gold stars

What your teacher writes back to you, and any gold star they give you.

Why: feedback, for you.
Who can see it: you and the teacher who wrote or gave it. A gold star is never shown to other students.

How your course measures learning

Letterman keeps a measure only if your course names one, such as a rubric level, a grade, a self-check or a reward. For each value it keeps the measure, the module, the value, who recorded it and when. A value your teacher records is seen by you and that teacher. A self-check you record is seen by you, and by your class's teacher only where your course says so; Letterman tells you which before you record it. As a guest, a self-check stays on this device, like your answers. What Letterman counts by itself, such as the steps you have done, is worked out on your device and never sent. Classmates never see any of it. It is in your export, and it goes when you delete your account; if your teacher deletes theirs, what they recorded for you stays with you, shown as from "your teacher".

What you write in the class's conversation

What you write goes to the class's conversation on Discord, under your display name and the words "via Letterman", posted by Letterman's own Discord app. It pings no one. Letterman itself keeps that you posted, to which module's conversation, when, and Discord's number for your message, never its words.

Why: so you can delete your post from Letterman, and so no one can flood the conversation: at most five posts in ten minutes.
Who can see it: your post, everyone who can read the class's conversation, on Discord or in Letterman; the record of it, only you.

If you teach

The classes you open, your announcements, your replies and the stars you give. While you teach a class live, which module and step it is on, until you end it.

Why: so you can teach.
Who can see it: you, and the students each one is for. While a class is open for joining, anyone, signed in or not, sees its title, its course, its start date, the time it meets, how many weeks it runs, its time zone, your display name and its announcements, and, while you teach it live, its module and step. Only you see who has joined and how many. Your account id is never shown to anyone. Only the person who runs Letterman's service can make someone a teacher; nobody can make themselves one.

Where it is kept

Letterman's service runs on Supabase, which stores its data. The person who runs Letterman's service can open that database to keep it working and to make someone a teacher. If you sign in with an email code, your email address passes through the email service that delivers the code. Like any website, the service also records technical logs of requests, such as when they happen and the internet address they come from.

The class's conversation is kept by Discord, and Discord's own rules apply there. A post you make from Letterman is posted by Letterman's app, not by your own Discord account, so you cannot delete it in Discord yourself. You can delete it from Letterman: open the conversation and choose "Delete my post". Your teacher can also remove it in Discord.

How long it stays

  • Until you erase it. A hand-in or an answer you delete is deleted at once.
  • When you delete your account, everything kept on it is deleted at once: your sign-in, your name, your two yeses, your classes, your progress, your work, and the replies and stars on your work.
  • If a teacher deletes a class, your own hand-ins and answers stay with you, and only you can see them.
  • If a teacher deletes their account, their classes, announcements and gold stars go with it. Their replies to your hand-ins stay with your hand-ins, shown as from "your teacher", with no link to the deleted account. Your own work stays yours.
  • If you teach and delete your account, the same is true of you: your replies stay with the students they were written to, without your name and without any link to you.
  • A sign-in that never said yes is erased within a day.
  • The record of a post you made in the class's conversation is kept while the post is on Discord, so you can still delete it. Once you delete the post, the record goes within a day.
  • When you delete your account, Letterman deletes your posts in the class's conversation on Discord first. If Discord will not delete one, Letterman tells you before anything goes, and you choose whether to go on.

Export and erase

In Settings and your data, inside Letterman (the account button at the top of every page), you can save a copy of everything kept on your account as a file, together with what this device keeps, and you can delete your account and everything kept on it. You do not need anyone's permission, and it cannot be undone, so save a copy first if you want one.

Questions

Ask your teacher, or ask in the class's Discord.
